rationale: Evidence: iteration 7 (score 929.76, best so far) finished 60/60 trials. Oval took 2.39 s, s-bend 2.44 s and slalom 2.63 s. Slalom max_error is 0.023 against an off-track limit of 0.06 m, so there is margin. The score is near its ceiling: 500 for completion, 250 for progress, about 105 from one line-loss event per run, about 65 from rms_error (about 0.011), and about 12 from time. Time is the cheapest remaining lever: each 0.1 s is worth about 2 points. Going from speed 1.0 to 1.1 gave only +0.4 points, so the trade is small but positive. Change: base_speed 1.1 to 1.2. I expect oval and s-bend to finish near 2.2 s and the slalom near 2.45 s, with slalom max_error rising only a few thousandths (about 0.03). That should add roughly 2 to 4 points. Everything else is unchanged (geometry, kp 4.5, ki 0.02, kd 1.0, sensor layout and weights, line_loss), so the effect of speed is isolated. Risk: slalom off-track exits at the higher speed. If slalom finishes fall below 20/20 or max_error exceeds about 0.04, revert to 1.1. Hypotheses: (1) the single line-loss event per run probably occurs at the start or finish when sensors leave the tape, so gains may not remove it; (2) s-bend rms (0.016) is the largest tracking term, and a slightly higher kd could reduce it if oscillation stays low. Measurements requested: completion, completion_time and progress to confirm the speed gain; line_loss_events to see whether it is a start or finish event; max_error and steering_oscillation to check slalom margin; rms_error to track the s-bend term.
